title: Cache Aware Scheduling Shows Nice Wins for AMD Zen 5 on PostgreSQL, Valkey
summary: This article from Phoronix benchmarks Cache-Aware Scheduling (CAS), a Linux kernel feature that intelligently places threads on CPU cores based on shared cache topology. Testing on AMD Zen 5 with PostgreSQL and Valkey workloads demonstrates measurable performance improvements by reducing cross-CCX cache traffic.
problem_solved: Traditional Linux schedulers lack awareness of CPU cache topology, causing suboptimal thread placement and unnecessary cache misses for workloads sharing data.
why_valuable: Cache-Aware Scheduling provides transparent performance gains for database and in-memory workloads by keeping cache-sharing threads co-located, requiring no application code changes.
